pulse.currentFocus: Session 333 restored The Desk to live publishing after a six-day, nine-run outage, and it took two independent fixes stacked in sequence. Topic selection gave up after one topic whose only direct source answered 401 while six readable topics sat untried; that repair then exposed a second failure it had been masking, where the managed inference provider had retired the pinned authoring model while still advertising it. The session also wired a regression self-test that had never been invoked by any runner into build:check, generalized its single-script assertion into a structural invocation-mode detector, repaired a public forge ledger that was publishing zero entries because a fixed 120-commit scan window had been buried by automation churn, and added consecutive-unknown streak plus last-known-good age to canonical destination evidence.
pulse.nextMilestone: Confirm unattended scheduled Desk runs keep landing editions, thread the authoring-model fallback into published story provenance, extend check-build-gate-reachability to every self-test-bearing module, and complete the founder-reserved Obelisk relying-party/passkey ceremony when available.
blockers: identity/auth surfaces remain held on real-provider-e2e-pending: obelisk.identity.verify is missing OBELISK_RP_ID, OBELISK_RP_NAME, and OBELISK_RP_ORIGIN; obelisk-staging-registration is also missing. The S332 candidate is blast-radius-disjoint and its scoped production resolver is allowed, which does not resolve or bypass this hold.

identity: the provider chain is live and verified (discovery JSON, authorize redirect, JWKS, and the revocation route all answer correctly as of session 321). The production promotion is held only on the real-provider journey, whose remaining leg is a founder passkey ceremony — hardware-key enrollment is founder-reserved by CANON-019 and is deliberately not automatable.
rollback architecture: the GitHub Pages warm origin still follows mutable main; D-S303 requires explicit founder authorization before migrating to an immutable verified generation.
IGNIS freshness: stale in a studio-ops portfolio artifact this repo cannot write; resolve upstream rather than backdating.
The Dispatch has zero confirmed subscribers until the founder clicks the double-opt-in confirmation email.

now: [S333][NEWS/P1] Confirm an UNATTENDED scheduled Desk run lands an edition. The 2026-08-31 edition proves the pipeline works, but it was manually dispatched under observation. The cron itself has not gone green unattended since 2026-08-29. Check the 06:07 / 12:07 / 18:07 / 22:07 UTC slots; if they still drop while a dispatch succeeds, the difference is environmental (scheduler context, token scope, or queue freshness), not the selection or model logic this session fixed.

[S333][NEWS/P2] Thread `fellBackFrom` into published story provenance. The inference layer knows which model authored and returns it, but the run log only says "authored on attempt 1" and the published day artifact does not record the model. With the preferred model depooled, editions are almost certainly standby-authored — and "almost certainly" is not a receipt. Persist the authoring model per story so AI-disclosure surfaces state a fact rather than an assumption.

[S333][NEWS/P1] Confirm the Desk publishes a real edition end to end on the standby model. ✅ Edition `2026-08-31` ("Meta's Data Center Robots: Tugger Carts and Laundry Folds") authored on attempt 1, promoted, deployed via content lane run `33356296320`, and verified serving HTTP 200; public freshness moved `periodic · age 6d` → `daily · age 0d`. Still open as a watch item below: this was a DISPATCHED run, not an unattended scheduled one. Original text: The selection fix is proven in production CI (`prepare: 0`, 2/2 sources, 6 sourced facts) and the model failover is proven live (`fellBackFrom` recorded, standby returns 200), but no edition has actually reached `/news/` yet. The proof is a scheduled run that goes green unattended and publishes a post-2026-08-30 edition. Until that happens the honest public state is still "periodic, latest 2026-08-25".

[S333][NEWS/P2] Watch whether Hetzner repools `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`, and review standby-authored editions for voice drift. The Desk prompts were tuned for Qwen3.6. Every standby-authored edition costs one wasted 503 round-trip (~500ms) and may read differently; if the retirement proves permanent, promote `Qwen3.8-27B` to primary and retune, rather than leaving a dead model as the declared preference.

[S333][OBS/P2] Alert when a provider advertises a model it cannot serve. `GET /models` listed the retired model as available, so no health check could distinguish "model exists" from "model is servable". A cheap periodic completion against each declared authoring model would have caught this before it stopped the newsroom.

[S333][INFRA/P2] The `full` derived-build profile is not full: it omits `build-public-status.mjs`, so a closeout cascade leaves the public status surface stale. `DERIVED_BUILD_PROFILES.full` is the profile `closeout-autopilot` runs after context write-back, but `build-public-status.mjs` appears only in `refresh-live-data`. Observed live in S333: after regenerating `public-intelligence` and running the `full` profile to green preflight, `build-public-status --check` still failed at build:check step 140 because nothing in `full` re-derived it. A profile named `full` that is a strict subset of another profile is a naming trap, and the cascade is only ever as wide as its declared graph. Either make `full` a genuine superset, or derive both profiles from one dependency graph so a consumer cannot be reachable in one profile and orphaned in the other. Pairs with the S333 invocation-mode work: same file, same class of gap.

[S333][OBS/P3] The Desk freshness banner disagrees with its own API by one day, and its `--check` gate goes stale daily by design. `news/index.html` embeds a rendered relative age ("latest published evidence 2026-08-25 · 6 days old") while `api/news-desk-freshness.json` and the scheduled cron both report `age 5d` for the same date on the same day. Two separate issues: reconcile the arithmetic (likely a ceil/floor or UTC-boundary difference), and decide whether a time-relative string belongs in a byte-checked static page at all — as built, `generate-news-pages --check` reports drift every single day purely from the clock, which trains readers of that gate to treat real drift as routine.

[S333][SIL][OBS/P2] Audit every other fixed-size scan window against current automation churn. The forge ledger went blind because it scanned a fixed last-120 commits while `[skip ci]` publishers commit several times an hour. Any other producer that samples "the last N commits/rows/lines" and then filters is vulnerable to the same burial. Enumerate them, re-size each by what it is looking for rather than by a raw count, and add a gate that fails when a noise-filtered producer yields zero entries while the repo has recent human commits — zero-with-activity is the signature, and it is currently indistinguishable from a genuinely quiet repo.
next: [NEXT][SIL][NEWS/AI/P1] Claim-evidence relationship map + agent critique packet. Add stable fact rows and validated factRefs joining factual evidence to stances and visual anchors; publish a per-story public-safe argument map and one-click critique packet with no runtime model spend.

[NEXT][SIL][OBS/P1] Field-vitals freshness closure. Surface observed-through/stale-days, restore a fresh post-S262 RUM window, and bind cohort verdicts to a release SHA so fresh generatedAt can never imply fresh field evidence.
